The data that looks like demand is mostly operator activity. First 2 minutes after graduation: 4,016 SOL bought by 20 buyers, with the top 5 accounting for 99.97% of buys and a launch bot present. Curve data shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 1.0. This matches the OPERATOR pattern, and that pattern has been roughly break-even, with no evidence of organic follow-through.

Last 15 minutes show 51 buyers and $12.8k volume, but net flow is only 67 SOL against 87 SOL bought, and 16 sellers are active. The 30-minute return of 8.6% and a drawdown of just 0.06% from the high are the strongest points, but a 30-minute high with a flat drawdown doesn't tell us whether the operators are still holding or preparing to exit.

I'd skip. Nothing here shows broad, organic demand that will persist 30-60 minutes out. The best available case rests on operator support, which the base rates don't reward, and a skipped coin costs nothing.

Those wallets have the cheapest entry and can sell into any retail bid. The recent 15-minute window shows 51 buyers against 16 sellers and net inflow of 67 SOL, but the sell_to_buy ratio of 0.0008 in the launch window and the 0.0006 drawdown from the 30-minute high mean the price has barely been tested. A single operator exit would drop price well beyond our 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost. Pool depth of 4,217 SOL is deep, but depth doesn't protect a buyer who enters after the operators have their bags. The 8.6% 30-minute return is what they would sell into. Skip.
